title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Managing the Process - Advertising
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: What is the primary legal purpose of posting a public notice or advertisement for a formal IFB or RFP?
options: To provide public notification ensuring a fair, transparent opportunity for all qualified vendors to compete
To inform internal departments of the procurement timeline
To survey the general public on budget usage
To permanently restrict international suppliers
questions.explain: Publicly advertising solicitations fulfills legal mandates for transparency and ensures that every interested, qualified vendor in the market has a fair opportunity to bid.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Most local and state statutes require an agency to advertise a formal solicitation for a minimum number of days before the bid opening. If a statute requires 14 days, when does this timeline officially begin?
options: The date the requisition is approved by finance
The date the solicitation document is first published/made available to the public
The date the first vendor downloads the document
The date of the mandatory pre-bid conference
questions.explain: Statutory advertising timelines start strictly on the first day the advertisement hits the designated publication (e.g., newspaper, eProcurement portal) making the document publicly available.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A buyer utilizing an eProcurement system sends direct email invitations to bid to a registered 'bidder's list.' To comply with full and open competition rules, the buyer must also:
options: Guarantee at least one vendor on the list wins
Ensure the opportunity is also posted publicly for any non-registered vendors to discover and participate
Charge a fee to any vendor not on the original list
Refuse bids from anyone who was not directly emailed
questions.explain: While directly inviting known vendors is a great sourcing practice, formal public procurement requires that the opportunity also be posted publicly so that unknown or new vendors have equal opportunity to compete.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When structuring a solicitation's outreach strategy, sending specific notifications to minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses is a practice associated with:
options: Supplier Diversity Programs
Qualification-Based Selection
Restricted Sourcing
Single Source Procurement
questions.explain: Supplier diversity initiatives encourage broad outreach to disadvantaged, minority, women, and veteran-owned business enterprises (M/WBE/DBE) to ensure they are aware of and participate in government contracting opportunities.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: To increase international competition, larger government procurements (especially federal or those using federal funds) may require publication in broad portals such as:
options: A local neighborhood newsletter
SAM.gov or specialized trade journals
The agency's internal intranet page
Social media groups exclusively
questions.explain: Large-scale procurements, particularly those subject to federal regulations or treaties, require publication in widely accessible, official centralized platforms like SAM.gov to ensure broad domestic and international access.
